I am an old woman now, seventy-two years, and my hands have worked this small piece of land for many seasons. I do not have money for the fertilizer from the shop — my neighbors here in Kigoma mostly do not use it either, and one bag is too much for my small plot anyway. I will put the manure from my few goats and chickens on the soil like I always do, and I will keep the seeds I saved from last harvest because they know this ground. My son helps me sometimes, and my grandchildren pull weeds, so I do not need to pay anyone.
